name: Samuel (Indian English)
sounds_like: Low male at 95 Hz, dark (centroid 1122 Hz), Indian English - retroflex consonants, syllable-timed rhythm, stress spread more evenly across words than in British or American English. Conversational 5.4 onsets per second with wide loudness swings (23.5 dB). 26.5s of shop-talk about notice periods and system-design interviews, so the delivery is relaxed and peer-to-peer.
casts_well_as: Indian English characters, colleague, engineer, friend venting, conversational drama, workplace scenes.
avoid_for: Roles written for other accents - the accent transfers from the reference and will not be neutralised by the text you give it.
note: Byte-identical to voices_examples/vibevoice/in-Samuel_man.wav; the in- prefix upstream means India, confirmed by the idiom in male_05_samuel.reference.txt (put in my papers).
